request.spec:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A cloned sheet now falls back to the rates of the sheet it was cloned from. If a grade has no rate in force on the sheet or its parents, the app looks at the source sheet, then that sheet's parents, then its own source, and so on. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V87__sheet_clone_source.sql`, adds a `sheet_source` table that records which sheet each clone came from. Like the parent setting, it isn't dated.
- **Clone:** `SheetClones.copy` writes that record when it creates the new sheet.
- **Rate lookup:** `Rates.lineage` now lists the sheet and its parents (up to 3 levels, as before), then repeats the same walk from the source sheet. It skips any sheet already in the list, so a loop of parents and sources can't make it run forever. The server's rate calculation and the rates endpoint both use this list, and the screen already works through the list by level, so the front end needed no logic change. I only updated the comments in `ratesQuery.ts` and `RateResponse.java` to describe the new order.

**Choices I made:**
- **Where the source walk applies:** only the sheet being looked at and its chain of sources get their source followed. A parent's own source is not checked. That's my reading of "a sheet that was cloned", and the tests don't cover the case where a parent was itself cloned.
- **Older clones:** sheets cloned before this change have no source recorded, so they behave as they did before.
